headline: Sanjō appears to be a Japanese coinage, 参 (san, “to come, to go”, humble connotations) plus 上 (jō, “up, upwards”).

headline: Heijō is from Middle Chinese 平常 and first appears in the 818 CE compilation 文華秀麗集 (Bunka Shūrei Shū).

headline: Yugamu is from Old Japanese, possibly related to 弓 (yumi, “bow”).

headline: Ore was originally a second person pronoun, as used in the Kojiki of 712 CE, and gradually became a first person pronoun.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. Originally a second person pronoun, as used in the Kojiki of 712 CE. Thought to have gradually changed into a first person pronoun from roughly the Kamakura and Muromachi periods. Some scholars, however, point out the lack of precedent of a second-person pronoun shifting to a first-person pronoun as an etymological discontinuity; they instead explain the first-person usage as an early corruption of 己 (onore, “I, me”), with the ancient second-person usage perhaps deriving of a different root.

headline: Nemutai is compared with 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), 眠い (nemui, “sleepy”) and おねむ (o-nemu), all related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”).

sources.quote: Compare 眠る (nemuru, “to sleep”), 眠り (nemuri, “sleep”), 眠い (nemui, “sleepy”), and おねむ (o-nemu, “(childish) sleepiness, sleep”), all ultimately related to Classical Japanese 寝 (nu, “to sleep”, modern 寝る (neru)).
